title: Dhuduki: a string beneath the story
lead: A small string instrument, a performer with several roles, and songs carried into public records: follow Dhuduki into Odisha’s theatre and musical life.

paragraphs: Begin with the string. Heritage Odisha’s account of Ghuduki Nabaranga Nata describes a hollow wooden cylinder, hide stretched across one end, and a string attached at its centre. The player holds the string with one hand and sets it sounding. The name Dhuduki leads us from this small instrument into a much larger world of sung theatre.

The interesting question is what the player does next. In the same account, the musician also directs, comments, jokes, dances and steps into the action. Following that performer offers a way to follow the whole telling.

blocks.title: An instrument inside the theatre
paragraphs: The essay describes performers changing roles among the spectators, with chorus and musicians joining the action as needed. It calls the form Ghudiki or Dhuduki Nabaranga Nata. These names connect an instrument to a theatrical practice; they do not mean every performance involving a similar instrument has the same cast or repertoire.

At a performance you are welcome to attend, watch the relationship between the player and the others. Who begins a passage? When does a character become a commentator? What does the group do when the instrument pauses? Those questions can reveal more than trying to recognise every word at once.

blocks.title: A name in a broadcaster’s record
paragraphs: AIR Cuttack’s music-artist roster gives Dhuduki Geeta its own heading. It lists Alok Bishoyi and party with an audition date of 2 March 2015. The table supplies a named research lead and a dated institutional record, rather than leaving the tradition as an anonymous category.

An audition date is not the date a tradition began. Nor does the listing establish a broadcast date, a recording we can hear, or the present availability of an artist. A useful next step would be to identify a credited recording or programme and keep its performers, song title and date together.

blocks.title: Keep the place with the name
paragraphs: Nayagarh’s district culture page lists Ghuduki with Ranapur. A separate fellowship report hosted by the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training names Ghuduki in its description of Patara Saura dance in the Gunpur region of Rayagada. These are distinct contexts in the sources; a shared instrument name is not enough to merge their performance traditions.

The report’s passage was available as indexed page text, but the full download could not be inspected in this research. It gives us a question to pursue with practitioners: what does this instrument accompany here, and what name do the players themselves use?

blocks.title: A history to investigate through people
paragraphs: The sources gathered here do not establish a founding date or a single birthplace for Dhuduki. An instrument description, a district list and a broadcaster’s roster illuminate different parts of its life. None supplies a complete history of how makers, teachers and performers passed it on.

For a closer account, begin with one player and one instrument. Ask who made it, who taught the playing, and which songs belong to that performer’s repertoire. Record the preferred spelling alongside the place and the person’s own explanation. Keep permission to listen separate from permission to record or publish.

That is the invitation of this story: stay with the musician long enough for the instrument to become part of a telling. This is a desk-researched introduction; no performance recording has been auditioned or reproduced.

sources.title: Heritage Odisha — Traditional People
sources.locator: Ghudiki (or Dhuduki) Nabaranga Nata section, three paragraphs. Descriptive cultural essay on the J K Dash website; publication date and original essay authorship not established. Construction and theatre roles attributed to this account, not independently observed.

sources.locator: Folk-dance list: Ghuduki (Ranapur). Page text read 15 October 2026; footer says last updated 10 June 2026. A locality association, not a performance schedule or origin claim.

sources.locator: Printed p.32, Patara Saura dance in the Gunpur region of Rayagada: Ghuduki named as an accompanying instrument. Indexed page passage inspected; complete PDF download timed out. Report date not established. Same publication identity as the Ghumura research, different passage.

listening_panel.note: Reading prompts; no field visit or recording is presented.

limits: Construction and theatre roles follow an attributed cultural essay, supported by distinct institutional records for musical category and locality. No original instrument, manuscript or recording inspected. CCRT evidence is limited to indexed page text. Origin chronology and local variations remain open; no independent human or practitioner review claimed.
